harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to serve DHCP on lan-a (10.50.10.0/24, gateway 10.50.10.1) via Kea DHCPv4, and node2 (OPNsense) to serve DHCP on lan-b (10.50.20.0/24, gateway 10.50.20.1) via dnsmasq. node3 (eth1, lan-a) and node4 (eth1, lan-b) already had NetworkManager configured for DHCP (ipv4.method auto) on their second NIC and now obtain their address and default route dynamically from their respective router rather than static config. All 4 nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot-identity changes confirmed and post-restart recovery verified (DHCP services active, static router-side addressing persisted across reboot, and both node3 and node4 automatically re-acquired the same leases with correct default routes to their segment's router).
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology via L2 ping tests: node1 eth2 <-> node3 eth1 (lan-a), node2 vtnet2 <-> node4 eth1 (lan-b), node1 eth1 <-> node2 vtnet1 (unrelated inter-router link, left untouched)
Configured VyOS node1: eth2 address 10.50.10.1/24, Kea DHCPv4 shared-network LAN-A subnet 10.50.10.0/24 with pool .100-.200, default-router 10.50.10.1; committed and saved

Investigated OPNsense node2's config.xml/model layer (Kea vs dnsmasq); discovered dnsmasq is the actually-running DHCP backend (Kea conflicted on port 67, address-in-use) so reverted the Kea subnet/enable change and instead added interface opt1 (vtnet2, 10.50.20.1/24) plus a dnsmasq dhcp_ranges entry (10.50.20.100-.200) via OPNsense's PHP model API, then applied via configctl interface reconfigure / template reload / filter reload / dnsmasq restart
Verified node3 and node4 acquire addresses and default routes automatically via their existing NetworkManager DHCP (auto) profiles on eth1
Captured pre-restart boot-identity baselines (boot_id / kern.boottime) and DHCP/service health for all 4 nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot, polled each until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot identity, and verified recovered DHCP service state and client leases/routes after each restart

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) serves lan-a addresses to node3 with itself as default route
evidence.summary: node1 eth2 set to 10.50.10.1/24, Kea DHCPv4 configured and active; node3 eth1 receives 10.50.10.100/24 with default route via 10.50.10.1

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) serves lan-b addresses to node4 with itself as default route
evidence.summary: node2 opt1/vtnet2 set to 10.50.20.1/24, dnsmasq configured with dhcp-range for vtnet2 and active on port 67; node4 eth1 receives 10.50.20.135/24 with default route via 10.50.20.1

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 obtain addressing dynamically (not statically) from the router in front of them
evidence.summary: Both node3 and node4 have ipv4.method=auto (DHCP) on their segment-facing NICs and confirmed dynamic lease acquisition with the router-provided default route

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id 7668189d before -> 0f6a05d5 after; Kea DHCPv4 active and eth2 IP persisted post-reboot; node3 retained working lease/gateway

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: kern.boottime changed from 04:22:27 to 04:41:39; opt1 static IP and dnsmasq service persisted/restarted post-reboot; node4 retained working lease/gateway

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id 8c28f3cd before -> 1ac94893 after; node3 automatically re-acquired 10.50.10.100/24 from node1 with correct default route after reboot

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id e65e6bcf before -> e531d838 after; node4 automatically re-acquired 10.50.20.135/24 from node2 with correct default route after reboot
